# Sprint Plan

## Sprint 1: Review the pull request in pr/

The change under review is `pr/head.diff` (unified diff, base to head). The files before the change are under `pr/base/`, after it under `pr/head/`; `pr/PR.md` is the pull request description and is the implementation report for this sprint.

### Tasks

- [x] Task 1.1: the change in `pr/head.diff`

### Review scope

The gates review `pr/head.diff` (pass `--diff-file pr/head.diff` to the adversarial review). Cite findings as `head/<path>:<line>` with lines from the `pr/head/` files.

## Success Criteria

review the pull request, report each defect it introduces with the file and line it sits on, and give a merge verdict
---
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:2390 — oracle detector skips every tool_result with is_error true, but Claude Code flags a non-zero Bash exit as is_error while keeping the output, and diff/sdiff/git diff --no-index exit 1 exactly when the files differ; a bare `diff pr/head/X X` (the canonical oracle probe) is never counted (AG-48 case 9 at head/evals/tests/ablation-grade.bats:1500 pins the wrong behaviour)
head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:210 — BASH_HDR admits `.` in the name and an optional brace, so zero-argument method calls (`out.pop()`, `conn.close()`) inside the Python heredocs that dominate this repo's .sh files register as bash definition headers and split the enclosing function's scope; reproduced: site and citation in the same function get no same-scope credit
head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:302 — Python close_line ends a definition at the continuation line of a multi-line signature (`def f(\n    x,\n):` → span is lines 1–2), excluding the whole body from its scope; reproduced: a citation in the body gets no same-scope credit
head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:478 — dissent_absent_reason maps an envelope with status api_failure (written directly by adversarial-review.sh with no recorded_by), refused, ceded, fold_failed or malformed_response to "none", so the dissent-absent sensitivity keeps the rows it is meant to exclude
head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:393 — the "disabled" reason is derived from the agent-writable sandbox/.loa.config.yaml, so an agent that flips flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled after a failed gate turns an error absence into a planned one; mount_integrity is not consulted
head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:1040 — oracle_closed clause (d) fails when rev-list --all is anything but the base commit, so any commit or stash the agent makes rows infrastructure_error and pauses the arm although no later blob entered the store
head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:214 — MD_HDR has no fence awareness, so `# comment` lines inside fenced bash blocks in .md files become level-1 headings and mis-split markdown scopes
head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:135 — the head-directory fallback is the agent-writable $workspace/pr/head; when ablation-grade.sh cannot resolve the fixture (EVAL_HEAD_DIR unset) the agent controls the validity rule and the scope map
head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:299 — the bash close check compares raw indentation while headers() uses expandtabs(8), so a tab-indented function never finds its closing brace
head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:287 — CLOSE_ONE treats a header whose trailing comment contains `}` as a one-line function
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1991 — the KF-046 exemption unit for a backticked token is the token itself, a substring of every fixture line holding it, so once the fixture names the repo anywhere any backticked mention is exempt regardless of context
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1570 — a numeric anchor on an extensionless path falls back to the finding's `file` (usually absent), so the citation is lost
head/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh:189 — under budget_scale diff, min(max(conf, ceil(est×1.2)), max) ≥ est whenever est ≤ max, so the gate reduces to est ≤ budget_cents_max and budget_cents / --budget / the 1.2 factor never affect the decision, contrary to how the docs present budget_cents
head/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh:164 — a yq read failure yields tag "unreadable", which sets CONF_BUDGET_SCALE_SET and logs a WARN naming the value "(a unreadable, not a string)", so the envelope names a scaling for a config that never wrote the key
head/.claude/schemas/adversarial-finding.schema.json:226 — metadata.status enum lacks budget_exceeded and the closed metadata object declares neither the new `reason` nor estimated_cents/budget_cents/estimate_voices, so the budget_exceeded envelope the gate writes violates the documented contract
head/evals/tests/ablation-grade.bats:1544 — AG-50 reads evals/tests/fixtures/c131-oracle/*, which this PR does not add; the test cannot run unless those fixtures already exist on the base
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

# Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor

<objective>
Audit code, architecture, infrastructure or sprint implementations for security and quality; produce prioritized findings with actionable remediation at the output path for the audit type.
</objective>

<zone_constraints>
## Zone Constraints

Three-Zone Model per CLAUDE.loa.md: `.claude/` system = never edit (use `.claude/overrides/` or `.loa.config.yaml`); `grimoires/loa/`, `.beads/` state = read/write; this skill's app zone (`src/`, `lib/`, `app/`) = **Read-only**.

Scope: app-zone files less the `.reviewignore` patterns (read it); `.claude/`, `grimoires/`, `.beads/` and `.run/` are excluded unless `--no-reviewignore` is passed.
</zone_constraints>

<integrity_precheck>
<!-- @skill-include: start integrity_precheck | hash:47b71a70 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/integrity_precheck.md -->
## Integrity Pre-Check (MANDATORY)

Before ANY operation, verify System Zone integrity:

1. Check config: read `integrity_enforcement` in `.loa.config.yaml`
2. If `strict` and drift detected -> **HALT** and report
3. If `warn` -> Log warning and proceed with caution
<!-- @skill-include: end integrity_precheck -->
</integrity_precheck>

<factual_grounding>
<!-- @skill-include: start factual_grounding | hash:edec7c58 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/factual_grounding.md -->
## Factual Grounding (MANDATORY)

Before ANY synthesis, planning, or recommendation:

1. **Extract quotes**: Pull word-for-word text from source files
2. **Cite explicitly**: `"[exact quote]" (file.md:L45)`
3. **Flag assumptions**: Prefix ungrounded claims with `[ASSUMPTION]`

**Grounded Example:**
```
The SDD specifies "PostgreSQL 15 with pgvector extension" (sdd.md:L123)
```

**Ungrounded Example:**
```
[ASSUMPTION] The database likely needs connection pooling
```
<!-- @skill-include: end factual_grounding -->
</factual_grounding>

<context_discipline>

Class: `.run/context-class` (`long` default; `standard` via `LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS=standard` or a
≤200K model). `.claude/protocols/tool-result-clearing.md` — long 20K/50K/30K/150K, standard 2K/5K/3K/15K (single /
accumulated / full file / session) → extract ≤10 files, ≤20 words, file:line to NOTES.md; reason
from it. Big files: `notes-guard.sh read --file F --section <H>` / `--index` first. Start: NOTES.md
"Session Continuity"; end / pre-compaction: update it.
<!-- @skill-include: end context_discipline -->
</context_discipline>

<trajectory_logging>
<!-- @skill-include: start trajectory_logging | hash:e809010f | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/trajectory_logging.md -->
## Trajectory Logging

Log each significant step to `grimoires/loa/a2a/trajectory/{agent}-{date}.jsonl`:

```json
{"timestamp": "...", "agent": "...", "action": "...", "reasoning": "...", "grounding": {...}}
```
<!-- @skill-include: end trajectory_logging -->
</trajectory_logging>

<grounding_requirements>
Read the actual implementation (never documentation alone) and cross-reference the technical-debt registry if one exists. Every finding cites the CWE/OWASP/CVE it violates with an absolute URL (not just the name) and quotes the vulnerable code inline. Where purpose or trust context (internal vs external) is unclear, state the assumption; say "Unable to assess" for obfuscated or inaccessible code and record scope limits in the report.
</grounding_requirements>

<workflow>
## Phase -1: Scope

Parallelise (`parallel_threshold`) when the scope warrants; the lead decides. A large scope splits per category (`<parallel_execution>`); otherwise run the 5 categories sequentially.

## Phase 0: Prerequisites Check

Sprint audit: `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/` exists and its `engineer-feedback.md` says "All good"; otherwise STOP: "Sprint must be approved by senior lead before security audit". With `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true`, its `adversarial-review.json` must carry `metadata.model` (the gate's `COMPLETED` check); otherwise STOP: re-run the review's Phase 2.5. Deployment audit: `grimoires/loa/deployment/` exists; read `deployment-report.md` for context if present. Codebase audit: no prerequisites.

## Phase 0.5: Scope Analysis

Run `.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh` before detailed analysis. It categorises the surface into Sources, Sinks, Auth and LLM/AI files.

## Phase 1A: Recon Pass

Catalog untrusted entry points and dangerous sinks without investigating yet (lists, trust levels: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Sources and Sinks). Track them in a working file, e.g. `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY_ANALYSIS_TODO.md`, with file:line, trust level and a status (`PENDING` → `CONFIRMED` / `SAFE` / `PARTIAL` / `N/A`) per item. On a large repo, prioritize by sink severity and reachability; cap entries, log the overflow.

## Phase 1B: Investigate Pass

Trace each flagged source forward to a sink or sanitizer (is the data validated/escaped first?) and each flagged sink backward to every source that reaches it (authorization and input-validation guards?), including second-order flows where stored data becomes dangerous on retrieval. Record each confirmed or dismissed path in the working file. If tracing outruns the time budget, mark the rest deferred, log it, and continue.

## Phase 1C: Security Dissenter Analysis

Runs when `flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` marker write (`adversarial-review-gate.sh`). Emergency override: `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes.

Run `.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --diff-range main...HEAD --json` — no `--context-file`. Two voices by default (`companion_voice`). Output: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`; one top-level bullet per rejected payload (`rejected_summary` or sidecar rows, whichever is more) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, else `verdict-derive.sh` fails the trailer. Mechanics: `resources/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md`.
Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never tallied; `metadata.locality.degraded_security_review: true` ⇒ state DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW.

## Phase 1: Systematic Audit

Execute by category (sequential, or split per Phase -1), each per its `resources/REFERENCE.md` section: **Security**, **Architecture**, **Code Quality**, **DevOps**, and **Blockchain/Crypto** when applicable.

## Phase 2: Report Generation

Use `resources/templates/audit-report.md`. Output stays in the State Zone: codebase audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY-AUDIT-REPORT.md` plus files under `remediation/` (Write creates it); sprint audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`; deployment audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/deployment-feedback.md`.

### Coverage

Report every finding you actually observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
the tally below is the filter, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line`, a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. Reserve
`critical` for a confirmed, exploitable path — it can never be excluded from the tally, so a
false positive there is the most expensive mistake in the report.

Every `critical` and `high` is tallied whatever its confidence, except a finding you mark
`speculative` with confidence `low`: list it under `## Observations`, leave it out of the tally,
and record the count in the trailer as `excluded` (a critical is never excludable). `medium` and
`low` are tallied and reported but never force the verdict. You do not decide the verdict; the
counts do.

Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under
`excluded`, either confirm it (still speculative, still low confidence) or tally it as a finding
of your own; record the confirmed count in the trailer as `excluded_confirmed`.

## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally (before the Verdict)

Count every finding from Phase 1 by severity into a literal table — `verdict-derive.sh` checks this against the trailer:

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | {N} |
| High | {N} |
| Medium | {N} |
| Low | {N} |

Severity calibration and worked examples: `resources/RUBRICS.md`. These counts drive the verdict below. One-way rule: `critical + high > 0` forces `CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does not itself force `APPROVED` — medium/low accumulation is still your judgment.

## Phase 3: Verdict

**Sprint/Deployment Audit:**
- If ANY CRITICAL or HIGH issues (per Phase 2.5 tally): "CHANGES_REQUIRED"
- If only MEDIUM/LOW: "APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO" (but note improvements)

**Codebase Audit:**
- Overall Risk Level: CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW
- Recommendations: Immediate (24h), Short-term (1wk), Long-term (1mo)

**LOA-VERDICT trailer**: append as the LAST line of the audit output file:
`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"audit","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"excluded_confirmed":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
(both extra fields may be omitted when 0). Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved
sprint/deployment audits use the exact prose `APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO`. `excluded_confirmed`
must equal the review trailer's `excluded`; the golden path refuses to advance otherwise.

**MUST self-check before finishing**: run
`.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh --file <audit-output-file> --gate audit --review-file grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-{N}/engineer-feedback.md`
and resolve any inconsistency before reporting completion.
</workflow>

<parallel_execution>
## Parallel Splitting (large scopes)

When splitting, use 5 parallel Explore agents — one per category (Security / Architecture / Code Quality / DevOps / Blockchain-Crypto) — each scoped to its category's files and returning findings with severity, file:line, and remediation (per-category file globs and prompts: see `resources/PARALLEL-SPLIT.md`). Consolidate: deduplicate overlaps, sort CRITICAL → LOW, take the overall risk from the highest severity present.
</parallel_execution>

<rubric_scoring>
## Rubric-Based Scoring

Score each dimension 1–5 per `resources/RUBRICS.md` (Security weighted highest; Blockchain when applicable), recording the findings that justify each score.
</rubric_scoring>

<structured_output>
## Structured JSONL Output

Alongside the markdown report, write machine-parseable findings to `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/findings.jsonl` per `resources/OUTPUT-SCHEMA.md` (the schema, each `reasoning_trace`, the closing summary record).
</structured_output>

<communication_style>
Be direct and specific, with evidence: "Line 47: user input passed unsanitized to eval(). Critical RCE. OWASP A03." — never "the code has security issues". Document blast radius, prioritize by exploitability and impact, suggest pragmatic fixes, and never defer a critical issue.
</communication_style>

<documentation_audit>
## Documentation Audit

For sprint audits, confirm each task has a documentation-coherence report (Glob `grimoires/loa/a2a/subagent-reports/documentation-coherence-task-*.md`; sprint level: `documentation-coherence-sprint-*.md`) or was manually verified — checks and red-flag tables: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Documentation. Blockers: an unverified missing report; uncommented security-critical code; a CHANGELOG omitting security changes; secrets or internal URLs in docs or comments; auth/crypto changes without security documentation; API changes that don't match the endpoint docs.
</documentation_audit>

<checklists>
Complete checklists for the five categories (Security, Architecture, Code Quality, DevOps, Blockchain/Crypto): `resources/REFERENCE.md`. Immediate CRITICAL red flags: private keys in code, SQL via string concatenation, user input to eval(), empty catch blocks on security code, hardcoded secrets.
</checklists>

<beads_workflow>
With `br` installed: `resources/BEADS-WORKFLOW.md` (sync, the audit comment, the `security*` labels, a discovered vulnerability).
</beads_workflow>

<retrospective_postlude>
<!-- @skill-include: start retrospective_postlude | hash:53d44248 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/retrospective_postlude.md -->
After the main skill logic, if `.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob invisible_retrospective.enabled`
prints `true` (and `invisible_retrospective.skills` does not disable this skill), silently run the
learning-signal scan per `.claude/skills/continuous-learning/SKILL.md` and its
`resources/RETROSPECTIVE.md` (quality gates, sanitization, trajectory logging). Never when the
active skill is continuous-learning itself.
<!-- @skill-include: end retrospective_postlude -->
</retrospective_postlude>

Cross-references removed from rule text: review-scope filtering (#303), dissenter anchoring-bias rationale and degraded-review marker (FR-2.5, FR-6.4), documentation-audit version tag (v0.19.0).

## Phase 0: Prerequisites Check

## Phase 0.5: Scope Analysis

Run `.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh` before detailed analysis. It categorises the surface into Sources, Sinks, Auth and LLM/AI files.

## Phase 1A: Recon Pass

Catalog untrusted entry points and dangerous sinks without investigating yet (lists, trust levels: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Sources and Sinks). Track them in a working file, e.g. `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY_ANALYSIS_TODO.md`, with file:line, trust level and a status (`PENDING` → `CONFIRMED` / `SAFE` / `PARTIAL` / `N/A`) per item. On a large repo, prioritize by sink severity and reachability; cap entries, log the overflow.

## Phase 1B: Investigate Pass

Trace each flagged source forward to a sink or sanitizer (is the data validated/escaped first?) and each flagged sink backward to every source that reaches it (authorization and input-validation guards?), including second-order flows where stored data becomes dangerous on retrieval. Record each confirmed or dismissed path in the working file. If tracing outruns the time budget, mark the rest deferred, log it, and continue.

## Phase 1C: Security Dissenter Analysis

Runs when `flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` marker write (`adversarial-review-gate.sh`). Emergency override: `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes.

## Phase 1: Systematic Audit

Execute by category (sequential, or split per Phase -1), each per its `resources/REFERENCE.md` section: **Security**, **Architecture**, **Code Quality**, **DevOps**, and **Blockchain/Crypto** when applicable.

## Phase 2: Report Generation

Use `resources/templates/audit-report.md`. Output stays in the State Zone: codebase audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY-AUDIT-REPORT.md` plus files under `remediation/` (Write creates it); sprint audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`; deployment audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/deployment-feedback.md`.

### Coverage

Report every finding you actually observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
the tally below is the filter, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line`, a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. Reserve
`critical` for a confirmed, exploitable path — it can never be excluded from the tally, so a
false positive there is the most expensive mistake in the report.

Every `critical` and `high` is tallied whatever its confidence, except a finding you mark
`speculative` with confidence `low`: list it under `## Observations`, leave it out of the tally,
and record the count in the trailer as `excluded` (a critical is never excludable). `medium` and
`low` are tallied and reported but never force the verdict. You do not decide the verdict; the
counts do.

Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under
`excluded`, either confirm it (still speculative, still low confidence) or tally it as a finding
of your own; record the confirmed count in the trailer as `excluded_confirmed`.

## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally (before the Verdict)

Count every finding from Phase 1 by severity into a literal table — `verdict-derive.sh` checks this against the trailer:

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | {N} |
| High | {N} |
| Medium | {N} |
| Low | {N} |

Severity calibration and worked examples: `resources/RUBRICS.md`. These counts drive the verdict below. One-way rule: `critical + high > 0` forces `CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does not itself force `APPROVED` — medium/low accumulation is still your judgment.

## Phase 3: Verdict

**Sprint/Deployment Audit:**
- If ANY CRITICAL or HIGH issues (per Phase 2.5 tally): "CHANGES_REQUIRED"
- If only MEDIUM/LOW: "APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO" (but note improvements)

**Codebase Audit:**
- Overall Risk Level: CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW
- Recommendations: Immediate (24h), Short-term (1wk), Long-term (1mo)

`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"audit","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"excluded_confirmed":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
(both extra fields may be omitted when 0). Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved
sprint/deployment audits use the exact prose `APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO`. `excluded_confirmed`

and resolve any inconsistency before reporting completion.

content.content:
# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (the PR description, `pr/PR.md`)
**Change under review:** `pr/head.diff` — feat(cycle-131): sprint-263 — closed review-catch mount, grader 1.3.0 with three results and an oracle detector, dissent line anchors + budget_scale, curated multi-site labels, versioned re-grade (35 files)

---

## Overall Assessment

The closed mount (`lib/sandbox-mount.sh` overlay, pre-launch check, took-effect `oracle_closed`), the budget scaling and numeric anchors in `adversarial-review.sh`, the report 1.3 partitions/sensitivities and the row writer 1.4 fields are well structured, heavily tested and, where I could run them, pass their suites: `sandbox-mount.bats` 11/11 (+1 skip), `eval-recall-grader.bats` 37/39 (the two failures need corpus fixtures absent from this snapshot), `ablation-report.bats` AR-48..AR-52 all pass (AR-33/AR-34 fail identically on the base tree, so they are pre-existing and environmental). `ablation-grade.bats`, `took-effect.bats`, `pipeline-run.bats`, `run-ablation.bats` and the two `tests/unit/*.bats` files need suite roots, run fixtures or helper libraries that are not in the PR snapshot and could not be executed here.

Three defects block the merge, all in the sprint's two headline graders:

1. The oracle detector's diff form discards every tool result flagged `is_error`, but Claude Code flags a non-zero Bash exit as `is_error` while keeping the output, and `diff` exits 1 exactly when the files differ. A bare `diff pr/head/X X` — the canonical oracle probe — is therefore never counted, and a test pins that behaviour as correct.
2. Grader 1.3.0's same-scope rule mis-detects bash function headers: any zero-argument method call (`out.pop()`, `conn.close()`) inside the Python heredocs that dominate this repository's `.sh` files registers as a bash definition and splits the enclosing function's scope. Reproduced: a site and a citation inside the same function, separated by such a line, get no credit.
3. The Python branch of end-of-definition detection ends a function at the continuation line of a multi-line signature (`def f(\n    x,\n):`), excluding the whole body from its scope. Reproduced.

Both grader defects move `recall` — the report's new decision statistic — silently, without any error. The `_pm3` results are unaffected.

The adversarial dissent ran with two voices (gpt-5.5-pro primary, claude-headless companion): one BLOCKING finding (item 3 above, verified) and four ADVISORY findings (item 2 above, verified and promoted; the other three recorded under Observations). No rejected payloads.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Oracle detector — the diff form never sees a differing `diff`

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:2390` — `oracle_scan` skips a `tool_result` whose `is_error` is true ("the tool failed … nothing printed"). `diff`, `sdiff` and `git diff --no-index` exit 1 when the operands differ, and the Claude Code transcript records a non-zero Bash exit as `is_error: true` with the output still in `content` (verified on this session's own transcript: `{"is_error":true,"content":"Exit code 1\n<output>…"}`). So the detector drops exactly the result that exposes the later copy; only a `diff` whose exit code is neutralised (`| head`, `|| true`, a loop whose last command succeeds) is counted.
**File:** `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:2390`; the behaviour is pinned as correct by `head/evals/tests/ablation-grade.bats:1500` (AG-48 case 9: a differing `20c20` result with `is_error` true must expose nothing).
**Issue:** The documented lower bound is far looser than described: the headline probe (`diff pr/head/.claude/x.sh .claude/x.sh`) is invisible, so `oracle_exposed_defects` under-reports and the report's oracle-exposed sensitivity (and `--exclude-oracle-exposed true`) keeps contaminated cells.
**Required Fix:** Treat `is_error` as "nothing printed" only when the content carries no diff body — e.g. skip when `content` is empty, or when every line matches `ERR_LINE` / `^Exit code \d+$`, and otherwise parse the content as today. Flip AG-48 case 9 to expect `diff=d1` and add a case with the Claude Code shape (`Exit code 1\n20c20\n< a\n---\n> b`, `is_error` true). Keep the skip for a hook block / refused command (content that is only the error text).

### 2. Grader 1.3.0 — a zero-argument method call is a bash function header

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:210` — `BASH_HDR[0]` is `^(\s*)(?:function\s+)?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]*\s*\(\)\s*\{?`: the name class admits `.` and the brace is optional, so `out.pop()`, `conn.close()`, `f.flush()`, `lst.sort()` match as definition headers. `headers()` (`:266`) runs on every line of a `.sh` file with no heredoc awareness, and this repository's harness scripts embed large Python heredocs (the grader itself has `out.pop()` at `:243`).
**Issue:** Reproduced with the head grader: a function `alpha() { python3 - <<PY … out.pop() … PY }`, defect site at line 5, citation at line 20 (both inside `alpha`) → `detected: []`, `credits_function_only: []`. The bogus header splits the real scope (deflation); an indented method call whose span is not clipped by a `}` at its own indentation also runs past the enclosing function's end and gives top-level sites a scope they should not have (inflation, per the dissent DISS-C-001). `recall` and `credits_function_only` drift from the documented rule without an error, in the dominant fixture file type.
**Required Fix:** Disallow `.` in the function name (`[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_:-]*`), require a `{` on the header line or as the first token of the next line, and clip each nested span to its enclosing span's end (`min(end, parent_end)`). Add an RG case with a Python heredoc containing `x.pop()` inside a bash function.

### 3. Grader 1.3.0 — a multi-line Python signature ends the function at line 2

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:302-309` — the Python branch of `close_line` returns `last` at the first later non-blank, non-comment line indented no deeper than the `def`. For `def check(\n    value,\n):` the `):` line has indentation 0 ≤ `lv`, so the definition is lines 1–2 and the whole body is top-level (scope `None`). Dedented lines inside multi-line string literals end the span the same way.
**Issue:** Reproduced with the head grader: site at line 6, citation at line 18 of such a function → `detected: []`. A citation inside the function body more than 3 lines from the site receives no same-scope credit, lowering `recall` and failing reviews that satisfy the documented rule. (Dissent DISS-001, BLOCKING, verified.)
**Required Fix:** Determine Python spans with `ast` (`FunctionDef.lineno`/`end_lineno`, `tokenize` fallback for files that do not parse), or at least continue the header through balanced parentheses to the line ending in `:` before applying the dedent rule. Add an RG case with a multi-line signature.

---

## Observations

### 1. Row writer 1.4 — dissent absence classification

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:478-479` — `reason()` maps an envelope to `budget` (status `budget_exceeded`), `preflight` (status or record-fallback reason naming it), `error` (status `failed` or `recorded_by: record-fallback`) and otherwise `none`. `adversarial-review.sh` writes `status: "api_failure"` directly (no `recorded_by`) when every hop fails (`head/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh` lines 1426 and 4739), and also `refused`, `ceded`, `fold_failed`, `malformed_response`; none of those contain "preflight", so such an envelope is rowed `dissent_absent_reason: none` ("the dissent ran"). The dissent-absent sensitivity then keeps exactly the rows it is meant to exclude.
**Suggestion:** Map `api_failure`, `malformed_response`, `refused`, `ceded`, `fold_failed` (and any status that is not `reviewed`/`clean`) to `error`, and add RW14-3 cases for them.

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:393-394` and `:466` — the `disabled` reason is derived from `$RUN_DIR/sandbox/.loa.config.yaml`, the agent-writable surface that `ablation-grade.sh`'s header calls tamperable. An agent that sets `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: false` after the gate failed turns `error` into a planned `disabled` absence; `mount_integrity` records the config change elsewhere but this field does not consult it. (Dissent DISS-C-002.)
**Suggestion:** Derive `disabled` from harness-owned evidence only (`dissent=false`, a mount-time copy of the config, or the gate flags `apply_arm_toggles` wrote), or honour the sandbox file only when `pipeline.json.mount_integrity.loa_config` reports it unchanged.

### 2. Closed mount — clause (d) and the agent's own git activity

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:1040` — `cmd_check` fails `oracle_closed` when `git rev-list --all` is anything but `[base_commit]`. Any commit or stash the reviewing agent makes in the sandbox (Loa skills `git add`/`commit`; `git stash` creates `refs/stash`) rows the trial `infrastructure_error` and pauses the arm (DEC-0418) although no later blob entered the store. The leakage signal that matters — the later-only pinned blob check at `:1050-1052` — stands on its own.
**Suggestion:** Keep "no remote, no alternates, no later-only blob" as the fail clauses; report extra commits/refs as evidence (or require only that `base_commit` is an ancestor of every ref) instead of failing the run.

### 3. Grader 1.3.0 — further scope-detection gaps

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:214` — `MD_HDR` (`^(#{1,6})(?:\s|$)`) has no fence awareness, so `# comment` lines inside fenced bash blocks in `.md` files (common in `.claude/**/*.md`) are level-1 headings: a site and a citation in the same prose section separated by a code block with a `#` line are in different scopes, and the heading hierarchy below the fence is reset.
**Suggestion:** Skip lines between ``` fences in `headers()` for markdown.

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: low) `head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:135` — the head-directory fallback is `$workspace/pr/head`, the copy the graded agent can write. `ablation-grade.sh` sets `EVAL_HEAD_DIR` only when `resolve_pr_fixture` succeeds (`head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1633-1634`); when it raises, the grader reads the sandbox copy (`grading/pr/head`) and the agent controls the validity rule (file length) and the scope map.
**Suggestion:** In `grade_recall`, fail the grade (GradeError) when the fixture does not resolve instead of letting the grader fall back; standalone use keeps the fallback.

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:299` — the bash close check compares `len(t) - len(t.lstrip())` with `lv`, but `lv` was computed with `expandtabs(8)` (`:283`), so a tab-indented function never finds its `}` and runs to the next header.

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:287` and `:295` — `CLOSE_ONE` (`\{.*\}\s*(?:#.*)?$`) reads a header like `f() {  # see } below` as a one-line function, since the `}` inside the comment satisfies the pattern.

### 4. Oracle detector and KF-046 exemption — smaller gaps

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1991` — for a backticked occurrence the exemption unit is the backtick span's content, which for `` `0xHoneyJar/loa` `` is the token itself and is a substring of every fixture line holding the token. # auditing-security — Security Dissenter (Phase 1C) detail

SKILL.md Phase 1C names the gate, the hook, the override and the invocation. This file carries
the merge rules and the failed-run record.

## Independence

The dissenter receives the diff only — never `--context-file` with your Phase 1A/1B findings —
so it evaluates the code without anchoring on your conclusions.

## Merging dissenter findings into Phase 2

1. CRITICAL/HIGH findings go into the audit report as findings of your own (they may change the
   verdict and must appear in the Phase 2.5 tally).
2. MEDIUM/LOW findings go under a "Cross-Model Security Observations" section.
3. A dissenter finding that duplicates one of yours is marked "Confirmed by cross-model review".

## Failed or unavailable dissenter

Output file: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`. The
`adversarial-review-gate.sh` hook checks that this file parses and carries `metadata.type` and `metadata.model` — a `--record-fallback` record names no model, so it never opens the gate: re-run the dissent (or the operator sets `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes). When `adversarial-audit.json` is ABSENT after the script exits — an aborted run leaves none: at start the script moves the previous round's envelope and sidecars aside as `.prev` and never restores them — record the failure with the script itself (a call this skill's allowlist holds; never a hand-written file):

```bash
.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --record-fallback failed --reason "<what happened>"
```

before proceeding. Branch on the `status` line the script prints on stdout, never on exit 2 alone (exit 2 with no status line is a usage error, or a standing envelope that stderr names):

- **An envelope stands after a run that took the run lock** — it is the script's own: triage it; never overwrite it.
- **`failed`** (no envelope: the run aborted) — the call above writes `{"findings": [], "metadata": {"status": "failed", "reason": "<what happened>", "rejected_summary": [], "rejected_sidecars": []}}` under the per-(sprint, gate) run lock. It never writes over an envelope that stands (exit 2), unless the run died before its lock with no status on stdout: what stands is then the previous round's — add `--since <the time on the run's "run started" stderr line>` and an envelope older than that goes aside as `.prev`.
- **`refused_concurrent_run`** (another run — a detached or backgrounded one — holds the run lock; nothing recorded, nothing moved; a `--record-fallback` made meanwhile is refused the same way) — wait until the holding run has exited: an envelope that then stands with a `metadata.timestamp` after your refusal is that run's: triage it as this round's dissent only when its `metadata.scope` is what you asked for (the same `diff_range` and `diff_oids` as your refusal's own `metadata.scope` — the commits, not just the ref names — and `run_tag` null: a chunk driver's tagged run reviewed one chunk); otherwise, or when none stands, run again.
- **`workdir_unavailable`, `nothing_to_review`, `budget_exceeded`, `diff_range_failed`** (the range's `git diff` failed — e.g. a base ref a shallow clone lacks; `workdir_unavailable` with `metadata.path` is a previous round's file that could not be moved aside — make the a2a directory writable; written BEFORE the run lock, or with it released; non-zero exit, stdout only; nothing moved aside, so any envelope at the path is the PREVIOUS run's and never this round's evidence) — record it: `--record-fallback <the status> --reason "<its stdout line>" --since <the run started time>` (it never displaces an envelope written after that) moves that envelope and its `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` sidecars aside as `<name>.prev` (as a run does at start) before it writes, so `verdict-derive.sh` judges this round's record, not the last round's.

A record names what it moved aside (`metadata.displaced`: status, timestamp, findings, rejected); `verdict-derive.sh` warns when that held findings. `verdict-derive.sh` never scans `.prev` files (they are the previous round's evidence, already triaged in that round's feedback) and reports `.prev` files with NO envelope as a `dissent_aborted` violation, which a fallback record clears; `rejected_sidecars: []` does not silence a canonical `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` beside it — that is this run's own partial work, counted whether listed or not: triage its rows under `## Rejected dissent payloads`.

Then set a `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker in the audit report. Empty
findings from a run that completed are a normal pass, not a degraded review.

A bare `planned: false` (the block opted out, `companion_voice: false`) is the operator's choice, not a degradation.
Otherwise a completed run is still a degraded audit when its second voice is missing: `companion_voice.status` `failed`
or `fold_failed`, `counted_as` `duplicate_voice` or `sole_voice`, or `planned: false` WITH a `reason` (a companion that
never started: `no_workdir`, `no_route`, `prompt_copy_failed`) — set the `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker and name the
reason. On a host with no route to the other family at all (`no_route`: no key and no CLI for it) that marker is set on
every audit; `companion_voice: false` on the block is the operator's way to say one voice is the host's shape.

## Two voices and the rejected-payload contract (cycle-126 FR-2)

**Companion voice (D-2.1).** Every dissent plans a second chain from the *other* provider
family — the primary configured on the block decides: any primary outside the Anthropic family (OpenAI,
Google, xAI, unknown) gets the Anthropic chain (`opus` → `claude-headless`), an Anthropic-family primary gets the OpenAI chain
(`gpt-5.5` → `codex-headless`; KF-002 keeps `gpt-5.5-pro` out of the default). Credential *presence* (env → `.env.local` →
`.env`; the value is never read) decides only where the companion chain starts — with no key it
starts at the CLI hop. Both chains walk in parallel; the two completed envelopes are aggregated
(`verdict_quality.voices_succeeded_ids` lists only completed voices). `companion_voice.status` is `succeeded`,
`failed` or `fold_failed`; `verdict_quality.voices_planned` counts the aggregated envelopes — 2 whenever the companion ran,
completed or not (a failed one is listed in `voices_dropped`) — except a failed companion whose id is one of the primary's
succeeded voices: INV-5 lets it feed no envelope, so `voices_planned` stays 1 and `companion_voice` is its only record; a `duplicate_voice` companion contributes none, and a
dropped entry naming the model the companion answered with is removed (INV-5). `companion_voice.counted_as`
(`independent_voice`, `duplicate_voice`, `sole_voice` — the primary never answered) names the outcome, and `planned: false` with a `reason` (`no_workdir`, `no_route`,
`prompt_copy_failed`) is a companion that never started; a bare `planned: false` is the opt-out. The
companion's findings arrive re-numbered `DISS-C-NNN` with a `voice` field; the primary's carry
`voice` too. `metadata.companion_voice` records `{planned, family, family_basis, chain, model,
status: succeeded|failed|fold_failed, failure_class: auth|model_unavailable|quota|timeout|lock_wait|malformed|null,
cost_cents, attempts}`; a companion whose chain fails is a dropped voice (degraded for an audit,
never blocking a review). Opt-out per block: `flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice: false`
(the YAML boolean spellings in any case; a value that is none of them is reported and the voice stays on).

**Tolerant schema (D-2.2).** A finding missing only `failure_mode` is no longer dropped: the
first sentence of its `description` (≤ 200 chars) becomes `failure_mode` and the finding is
marked `failure_mode_derived: true` (a missing `id` is filled positionally, `id_derived: true`).
Severity, category and description are never touched. Payloads that still fail go to the
sidecar (`adversarial-rejected-<type>.jsonl`, `-companion` suffix for the second voice) **and**
to `metadata.rejected_summary[]` as `{index, severity, title, title_derived, anchor, reason, description_head}`.

**The contract (D-2.3).** When `rejected_summary` is non-empty the feedback file MUST contain a
`## Rejected dissent payloads` section with one line per entry — `- <title> (<severity>, <anchor>)
— <reason>: triaged as <real defect → counted under the matching heading | not a defect → why>`.
`verdict-derive.sh` reads the sibling envelope (`adversarial-<gate>.json`, or `--envelope <path>`)
and marks the trailer INCONSISTENT (exit 1) when the section is missing. Reading a sidecar row:
`payload` is the model's finding as normalised, `reject_reason` the clause it failed, and
`repair_attempted` / `repair_succeeded` whether the bounded repair round-trip ran.

**Round-1 hardening (sprint-248 review, sixteen live two-voice runs).** One list, by envelope field; both skills' copies of
this block are kept byte-identical (CMP-138 fails on any drift).

- **Two voices, one envelope.** The companion runs in its own sub-workdir with a log and its own copies of the prompt files.
  The envelope's `cost_usd` / tokens are BOTH voices; the per-voice spend stays under `companion_voice.cost_cents`, and
  `budget_cents` is a per-voice cap (a malformed cap is 0 cents — the run fails closed with `status: budget_exceeded`).

SKILL.md Phase 1C names the gate, the hook, the override and the invocation. This file carries
the merge rules and the failed-run record.

## Independence

The dissenter receives the diff only — never `--context-file` with your Phase 1A/1B findings —
so it evaluates the code without anchoring on your conclusions.

## Merging dissenter findings into Phase 2

1. CRITICAL/HIGH findings go into the audit report as findings of your own (they may change the
   verdict and must appear in the Phase 2.5 tally).
2. MEDIUM/LOW findings go under a "Cross-Model Security Observations" section.
3. A dissenter finding that duplicates one of yours is marked "Confirmed by cross-model review".

## Failed or unavailable dissenter

Output file: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`. The
`adversarial-review-gate.sh` hook checks that this file parses and carries `metadata.type` and `metadata.model` — a `--record-fallback` record names no model, so it never opens the gate: re-run the dissent (or the operator sets `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes). When `adversarial-audit.json` is ABSENT after the script exits — an aborted run leaves none: at start the script moves the previous round's envelope and sidecars aside as `.prev` and never restores them — record the failure with the script itself (a call this skill's allowlist holds; never a hand-written file):

```bash
.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --record-fallback failed --reason "<what happened>"
```

before proceeding. Branch on the `status` line the script prints on stdout, never on exit 2 alone (exit 2 with no status line is a usage error, or a standing envelope that stderr names):

- **An envelope stands after a run that took the run lock** — it is the script's own: triage it; never overwrite it.
- **`failed`** (no envelope: the run aborted) — the call above writes `{"findings": [], "metadata": {"status": "failed", "reason": "<what happened>", "rejected_summary": [], "rejected_sidecars": []}}` under the per-(sprint, gate) run lock. It never writes over an envelope that stands (exit 2), unless the run died before its lock with no status on stdout: what stands is then the previous round's — add `--since <the time on the run's "run started" stderr line>` and an envelope older than that goes aside as `.prev`.
- **`refused_concurrent_run`** (another run — a detached or backgrounded one — holds the run lock; nothing recorded, nothing moved; a `--record-fallback` made meanwhile is refused the same way) — wait until the holding run has exited: an envelope that then stands with a `metadata.timestamp` after your refusal is that run's: triage it as this round's dissent only when its `metadata.scope` is what you asked for (the same `diff_range` and `diff_oids` as your refusal's own `metadata.scope` — the commits, not just the ref names — and `run_tag` null: a chunk driver's tagged run reviewed one chunk); otherwise, or when none stands, run again.

+            continue
+        if line.startswith("diff --git "):
+            out.extend(strip_prefix(x) for x in header_names(line[len("diff --git "):]))
+            continue
+        for key in ("rename from ", "rename to ", "copy from ", "copy to "):
+            if line.startswith(key):
+                out.append(one_name(line[len(key):]))
+                break
+        else:
+            if line.startswith("--- ") or line.startswith("+++ "):
+                v = line[4:]
+                if not v.startswith('"'):
+                    v = v.split("\t", 1)[0]
+                out.append(strip_prefix(one_name(v)))
+                continue

+            if m:
+                out.extend(strip_prefix(one_name(x)) for x in (m.group(1), m.group(2)))

+def tree_paths(root):
+    out = set()
+    if not os.path.isdir(root) or os.path.islink(root):
+        return out
+    for d, dirs, files in os.walk(root, followlinks=False):
+        for n in dirs + files:
+            full = os.path.join(d, n)
+            if os.path.islink(full) or os.path.isfile(full):
+                out.add(os.path.relpath(full, root).replace(os.sep, "/"))
+    return out

+def fixture_meta(fixture):
+    meta = {}
+    f = os.path.join(fixture, "fixture.yaml")
+    if os.path.isfile(f):
+        for line in open(f, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
+            m = re.match(r'^(head_commit|fix_commit|base_commit):\s*["\']?([0-9a-f]{7,64})["\']?\s*(#.*)?$', line.strip())
+            if m:
+                meta[m.group(1)] = m.group(2)
+    return meta
+
+def in_scope(p):
+    return p is not None and p.startswith(".claude/") and p != ".claude/checksums.json"
+
+def answer_set(fixture, repo):
+    """{path: "pr"|"fix"}, notes, meta"""
+    notes = []
+    if not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(fixture, "head.diff")):
+        die("fixture has no head.diff: " + fixture)
+    pr = set()
+    for raw in diff_paths(os.path.join(fixture, "head.diff")) + sorted(tree_paths(os.path.join(fixture, "head"))) \
+            + sorted(tree_paths(os.path.join(fixture, "base"))):
+        if raw is None:
+            continue
+        p = norm(raw)
+        if p is None:
+            notes.append("rejected path %r" % raw)
+            continue
+        pr.add(p)
+    meta = fixture_meta(fixture)
+    fix = set()
+    fc = meta.get("fix_commit")
+    meta["fix_available"] = "none"
+    if fc:
+        out = git(repo, "show", "--no-renames", "--name-only", "-z", "--format=", fc) if has_commit(repo, fc) else None
+        if out is None:
+            notes.append("fix_commit_unavailable " + fc)
+            meta["fix_available"] = "unavailable"
+        else:
+            meta["fix_available"] = "available"
+            for raw in out.decode("utf-8", "surrogateescape").split("\0"):
+                raw = raw.strip("\n")
+                if not raw:
+                    continue
+                p = norm(raw)
+                if p is None:
+                    notes.append("rejected fix path %r" % raw)
+                    continue
+                fix.add(p)
+    hc = meta.get("head_commit")
+    meta["head_available"] = bool(hc) and has_commit(repo, hc)
+    entries = {}
+    for p in sorted(pr | fix):
+        if in_scope(p):
+            entries[p] = "pr" if p in pr else "fix"
+    return entries, notes, meta
+
+def fixture_file(root, path):
+    """(bytes, exec) of a regular file at root/path with no symlink component, else None"""
+    cur = root
+    if os.path.islink(cur) or not os.path.isdir(cur):
+        return None
+    parts = path.split("/")
+    for c in parts:
+        cur = os.path.join(cur, c)
+        if os.path.islink(cur):
+            return None
+    try:
+        st = os.lstat(cur)
+    except OSError:
+        return None
+    if not stat.S_ISREG(st.st_mode):
+        return None
+    return open(cur, "rb").read(), bool(st.st_mode & 0o111)
+
+def tree_blob(repo, commit, path):
+    """(bytes, exec, blob_id) of a regular-file entry in commit, else None"""
+    out = git(repo, "ls-tree", "-z", commit, "--", path)
+    if not out:
+        return None
+    ent = out.split(b"\0")[0].decode("utf-8", "surrogateescape")
+    m = re.match(r"^(\d+) (\w+) ([0-9a-f]+)\t(.*)$", ent, re.S)
+    if not m or m.group(2) != "blob" or m.group(4) != path or m.group(1) not in ("100644", "100755"):
+        return None
+    data = git(repo, "cat-file", "blob", m.group(3))
+    if data is None:
+        return None
+    return data, m.group(1) == "100755", m.group(3)
+
+def expected(entries, mode, fixture, repo, meta):
+    """{path: (bytes, exec) | None}"""
+    exp = {}
+    for p, src in entries.items():
+        if src == "pr":
+            exp[p] = fixture_file(os.path.join(fixture, mode), p)
+        elif meta.get("head_available"):
+            tb = tree_blob(repo, meta["head_commit"], p)
+            exp[p] = (tb[0], tb[1]) if tb else None
+        else:
+            exp[p] = None
+    return exp
+
+def state(ws, path):
+    """sha256 of the sandbox file, 'absent', or a non-file marker (never followed)"""
+    cur = ws
+    for c in path.split("/")[:-1]:
+        cur = os.path.join(cur, c)
+        if os.path.islink(cur):
+            return "symlink-component"
+    full = os.path.join(ws, *path.split("/"))
+    if os.path.islink(full):
+        return "symlink"
+    if not os.path.lexists(full):
+        return "absent"
+    if not os.path.isfile(full):
+        return "not-a-file"
+    return sha(open(full, "rb").read())
+
+def safe_dst(ws, path):
+    cur = ws
+    for c in path.split("/")[:-1]:
+        cur = os.path.join(cur, c)
+        if os.path.islink(cur):
+            die("overlay refused: symlink component %s in the sandbox path of %s" % (os.path.relpath(cur, ws), path))
+        if os.path.lexists(cur) and not os.path.isdir(cur):
+            die("overlay refused: non-directory component %s in the sandbox path of %s" % (os.path.relpath(cur, ws), path))
+    return os.path.join(ws, *path.split("/"))
+
+def remove(dst):
+    if os.path.islink(dst) or (os.path.lexists(dst) and not os.path.isdir(dst)):
+        os.unlink(dst)
+    elif os.path.isdir(dst):
+        shutil.rmtree(dst)

+    return bool(re.match(r"^\.claude/(scripts|hooks)/", p) or re.match(r"^\.claude/skills/[^/]+/SKILL\.md$", p))

+def cmd_overlay(ws, fixture, mode, repo):
+    if mode not in ("head", "base"):
+        die("overlay mode must be head or base, got %r" % mode)
+    if not os.path.isdir(ws) or os.path.islink(ws):
+        die("workspace not found: " + ws)
+    entries, notes, meta = answer_set(fixture, repo)
+    exp = expected(entries, mode, fixture, repo, meta)
+    for n in notes:
+        note("overlay: " + n)
+    if entries and any(s == "fix" for s in entries.values()) and not meta.get("head_available"):
+        note("overlay: head_commit %s unavailable: fix-commit paths outside the PR are removed" % meta.get("head_commit"))
+    lines, gates, removed = [], [], 0
+    for p in sorted(entries):

+        e = exp[p]
+        remove(dst)

+def read_evidence(f):

+_sm_copy_source() {
+  local tree="$1" head dirty
+  head="$(git -C "$tree" rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null)" || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }
+  [[ "$head" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }

+def result_text(blk):

+def ranges_of(text, sides=("left", "right")):
+    """the printed line ranges of a unified or normal diff on the given sides (left = first operand)"""
+    rs = []
+    for m in HUNK_U.finditer(text):
+        a, n = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2) or 1)
+        c, k = int(m.group(3)), int(m.group(4) or 1)
+        if "left" in sides:
+            rs.append((a, a + max(n, 1) - 1))
+        if "right" in sides:
+            rs.append((c, c + max(k, 1) - 1))
+    for m in HUNK_N.finditer(text):
+        a = int(m.group(1))
+        c = int(m.group(4))
+        if "left" in sides:
+            rs.append((a, int(m.group(2) or a)))
+        if "right" in sides:
+            rs.append((c, int(m.group(5) or c)))

+def sections(text, targets):
+    """{target: [section body]}: the result split at header lines — a diff header (diff, ---, +++, ***) or
+    a line that is not diff body and names a file (an `echo "=== $f"` marker); a header naming a target
+    (the longest one it holds) opens that target's section, any other header a dropped one; text before
+    the first header belongs to the sole target. Text no header attributes (several targets) is returned
+    as the loose list. Header lines are not part of a body. → (sections, loose)"""
+    out = {f: [] for f in targets}
+    loose = []
+    cur = targets[0] if len(targets) == 1 else None
+    buf = []
+
+    def flush():
+        if buf:
+            (out[cur] if cur is not None else loose).append("\n".join(buf))
+
+    for line in text.split("\n"):
+        diff_hdr = line.startswith(("diff ", "--- ", "*** ", "+++ "))
+        if diff_hdr or (not DIFF_BODY.match(line) and FILEISH.search(line)):
+            named = sorted((f for f in targets if f in line), key=len, reverse=True)
+            hit = named[0] if named else None
+            if line.startswith("+++ ") and hit == cur:
+                continue
+            if hit is not None or diff_hdr or len(targets) > 1:
+                flush()
+                buf = []
+                cur = hit
+                continue
+        buf.append(line)
+    flush()
+    return out, loose

+def oracle_scan(t, run_dir):
+    try:
+        pr = resolve_pr_fixture(t)
+    except GradeError:

+    answer = answer_paths(pr)

+            mm = (d.get("must_match") or "").strip()[:50] if isinstance(d.get("must_match"), str) else ""
+            by_file.setdefault(f, []).append((f"d{i}", sites, mm if len(mm) >= 12 else ""))
+    if not by_file:

+    sb = os.path.join(run_dir, "sandbox")

+        bs = read_regular(os.path.join(pr, "base", *f.split("/")), FILE_CAP, root=pr)
+        live[f] = cur is not None and cur != hd and cur != bs
+        later[f] = []
+        if not live[f] or hd is None:

+        for pos, sites, _mm in by_file[f]:
+            near_text[(f, pos)] = [hl[L - 1].strip() for s_ in sites for L in range(s_ - 3, s_ + 4)
+                                   if 1 <= L <= len(hl) and len(hl[L - 1].strip()) >= 8]
+        known = set(x.strip() for x in hl) | (set(x.strip() for x in bs.split("\n")) if bs is not None else set())
+        for tag, i1, i2, j1, j2 in difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, hl, cl, autojunk=False).get_opcodes():
+            if tag == "equal":

+            lo, hi = i1 + 1, max(i2, i1 + 1)

+    def near(sites, lo, hi):

+        for i, line in enumerate(open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), 1):
+            try:
+                ev = json.loads(line)
+            except ValueError:
+                continue
+            if not isinstance(ev, dict):
+                continue
+            if ev.get("type") == "system" and isinstance(ev.get("cwd"), str) and ev["cwd"].startswith("/"):
+                ws = os.path.normpath(ev["cwd"])
+                continue
+            content = (ev.get("message") or {}).get("content") if isinstance(ev.get("message"), dict) else None
+            if not isinstance(content, list):
+                continue

+                if not isinstance(blk, dict):

+                    if plan and isinstance(blk.get("id"), str):
+                        uses[blk["id"]] = (i, plan)
+                elif ev.get("type") == "user" and blk.get("type") == "tool_result" and blk.get("tool_use_id") in uses:
+                    i0, plan = uses.pop(blk["tool_use_id"])
+                    if blk.get("is_error") is True:
+                        continue          # the tool failed (a refused command, a hook block): nothing printed
+                    res = result_text(blk)
+                    dtargets = sorted({f for how, f in plan if how.startswith("diff") and live.get(f)})

+    ex = sorted(exposed, key=order.get)
+    unk = sorted((p for p in unknown if p not in exposed), key=order.get)
+    events.sort(key=lambda e: (ORACLE_PHASES.index(e["phase"]), e["event"], e["how"], e["path"]))

+            vars_[m.group(1)] = words
+            continue
+        if not w:
+            continue
+        exe = w[0].rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
+        if exe == "cd" and len(w) >= 2:
+            vals = expand(w[1], vars_)
+            if vals:
+                cwd = os.path.normpath(vals[0] if vals[0].startswith("/") else os.path.join(cwd, vals[0]))
+            continue

+                      and ws_targets(c[1], answer, True)]

+                side = ("left" if heads[0] < ws_ops[0] else "right") if heads else "both"
+                out += [("diff:" + side, f) for f in targets]

+# throwaway source repository (the pinned Loa tree: a head commit, then a fix commit
+# that is the pin), a PR fixture (head.diff, head/, base/, fixture.yaml) whose head.diff
+# carries every path shape (modified, added, deleted, renamed, a quoted path with a
+# space, a symlink in head, a path outside .claude/, a removed hunk line that looks like
+# a header, a binary hunk), and a sandbox built as pipeline-run.sh builds it (pr/ copied,
+# a base commit, the whole .claude/ mounted). Also the cycle-131 toggles (bare_model,
+# dissent, oracle_open) and the eval config variant. No model call, no docker.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
+  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
+  LIB="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh"
+  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sm.XXXXXX")"
+  SRC="$T/src" FX="$T/fx" W="$T/ws"
+  export ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE="$T/ev.txt"; : > "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE"
+  make_source
+  make_fixture
+  make_ws
+}
+
+teardown() {
+  chmod -R u+rwx "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
+  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
+  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
+}
+
+g() { git -C "$1" -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t -c commit.gpgsign=false "${@:2}"; }
+
+# the pinned Loa tree: commit H (= the PR's head_commit) then commit F (the fix, the pin)
+make_source() {
+  mkdir -p "$SRC/.claude/scripts" "$SRC/.claude/data" "$SRC/.claude/loa" "$SRC/.claude/skills/s1" "$SRC/lib"
+  printf 'mod head\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/mod.sh"
+  printf 'added head\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/added.sh"
+  printf 'new name head\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/new name.sh"
+  printf 'xy head\n' > "$SRC/.claude/data/x y.txt"
+  printf 'fixonly head\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/fixonly.sh"
+  printf 'skill pinned\n' > "$SRC/.claude/skills/s1/SKILL.md"
+  printf 'loa\n' > "$SRC/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+  printf 'outside head\n' > "$SRC/lib/outside.sh"
+  printf '{"files":{}}\n' > "$SRC/.claude/checksums.json"
+  chmod +x "$SRC/.claude/scripts/mod.sh"
+  ( cd "$SRC" && git init -q && g . add -A && g . commit -qm head )
+  H="$(git -C "$SRC" rev-parse HEAD)"
+  # the fix commit: later versions of PR paths and of a path the PR never touched
+  printf 'mod LATER fixed\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/mod.sh"
+  printf 'added LATER fixed\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/added.sh"
+  printf 'deleted LATER restored\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/deleted.sh"
+  printf 'new name LATER\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/new name.sh"
+  printf 'xy LATER\n' > "$SRC/.claude/data/x y.txt"
+  printf 'fixonly LATER fixed\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/fixonly.sh"
+  printf '{"files":{"later":1}}\n' > "$SRC/.claude/checksums.json"
+  ( cd "$SRC" && g . add -A && g . commit -qm fix )
+  F="$(git -C "$SRC" rev-parse HEAD)"
+}
+
+# the PR fixture (immutable in production: evals/fixtures/review-prs/pr-NN/)
+make_fixture() {
+  mkdir -p "$FX/head/.claude/scripts" "$FX/head/.claude/data" "$FX/head/.claude/skills/s1" "$FX/head/lib" \
+           "$FX/base/.claude/scripts" "$FX/base/.claude/data" "$FX/base/lib"
+  printf 'mod head\n' > "$FX/head/.claude/scripts/mod.sh"; chmod +x "$FX/head/.claude/scripts/mod.sh"
+  printf 'mod base\n' > "$FX/base/.claude/scripts/mod.sh"
+  printf 'added head\n' > "$FX/head/.claude/scripts/added.sh"
+  printf 'deleted base\n' > "$FX/base/.claude/scripts/deleted.sh"
+  printf 'old name base\n' > "$FX/base/.claude/scripts/old name.sh"
+  printf 'new name head\n' > "$FX/head/.claude/scripts/new name.sh"
+  printf 'xy head\n' > "$FX/head/.claude/data/x y.txt"
+  printf 'xy base\n' > "$FX/base/.claude/data/x y.txt"
+  printf 'SECRET outside the fixture\n' > "$T/outside-secret"
+  ln -s ../../../../outside-secret "$FX/head/.claude/skills/s1/SKILL.md"
+  printf 'outside head\n' > "$FX/head/lib/outside.sh"; printf 'outside base\n' > "$FX/base/lib/outside.sh"
+  cat > "$FX/head.diff" <<'DIFF'
+diff --git a/.claude/scripts/mod.sh b/.claude/scripts/mod.sh
+--- a/.claude/scripts/mod.sh
++++ b/.claude/scripts/mod.sh
+@@ -1,2 +1,1 @@
+--- a/.claude/scripts/evil.sh
+-mod base
++mod head
+diff --git a/.claude/scripts/added.sh b/.claude/scripts/added.sh
+new file mode 100644
+--- /dev/null
++++ b/.claude/scripts/added.sh
+@@ -0,0 +1 @@
++added head
+diff --git a/.claude/scripts/deleted.sh b/.claude/scripts/deleted.sh
+deleted file mode 100644
+--- a/.claude/scripts/deleted.sh
++++ /dev/null
+@@ -1 +0,0 @@
+-deleted base
+diff --git a/.claude/scripts/old name.sh b/.claude/scripts/new name.sh
+similarity 50%
+rename from .claude/scripts/old name.sh
+rename to .claude/scripts/new name.sh
+diff --git "a/.claude/data/x y.txt" "b/.claude/data/x y.txt"
+--- "a/.claude/data/x y.txt"
++++ "b/.claude/data/x y.txt"
+@@ -1 +1 @@
+-xy base
++xy head
+diff --git a/.claude/assets/logo.png b/.claude/assets/logo.png
+new file mode 100644
+Binary files /dev/null and b/.claude/assets/logo.png differ
+diff --git a/lib/outside.sh b/lib/outside.sh
+--- a/lib/outside.sh
++++ b/lib/outside.sh
+@@ -1 +1 @@
+-outside base
++outside head
+DIFF
+  printf 'name: pr-t\nbase_commit: "%s"\nhead_commit: "%s"\nfix_commit: "%s"\n' "$H" "$H" "$F" > "$FX/fixture.yaml"
+}
+
+# the sandbox as pipeline-run.sh materialises it: pr/, the base commit, then the mount
+make_ws() {
+  mkdir -p "$W/pr"
+  cp -a "$FX/base" "$FX/head" "$FX/head.diff" "$W/pr/"
+  git -C "$W" init -q
+  printf '%s\n' '/.claude/' '/CLAUDE.md' '/.loa.config.yaml' '/grimoires/' '/.run/' '/.beads/' '/.eval/' >> "$W/.git/info/exclude"
+  g "$W" add -A; g "$W" commit -qm base
+  printf 'base_commit=%s\n' "$(git -C "$W" rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE"
+  mkdir -p "$W/.claude"; cp -a "$SRC/.claude/." "$W/.claude/"
+  printf 'flatline_protocol:\n  enabled: true\n  code_review:\n    enabled: true\n  security_audit:\n    enabled: true\n' > "$W/.loa.config.yaml"
+}
+
+# lib <fn> <args…> — run one library function in a fresh shell (the library sets no options)
+lib() { run bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; source "$1"; shift; "$@"' _ "$LIB" "$@"; }
+ev() { grep -E "^$1=" "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE" | sed "s/^$1=//"; }
+content() { cat "$W/$1"; }
+
+@test "answer set: diff headers (quoted, renamed both names, /dev/null, binary), head/ and base/ files, fix-commit paths; only .claude/, never checksums.json, a removed '--- a/' line or a path outside .claude/" {
+  lib _sm_oracle_py answer-set "$FX" "$SRC"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  want=$'pr\t.claude/assets/logo.png\npr\t.claude/data/x y.txt\npr\t.claude/scripts/added.sh\npr\t.claude/scripts/deleted.sh\nfix\t.claude/scripts/fixonly.sh\npr\t.claude/scripts/mod.sh\npr\t.claude/scripts/new name.sh\npr\t.claude/scripts/old name.sh\npr\t.claude/skills/s1/SKILL.md'
+  [ "$(grep -v '^sandbox-mount:' <<<"$output")" = "$want" ]
+}
+
+@test "answer set: a CRLF head.diff and a C-quoted octal path parse the same; an unsafe path is rejected" {
+  local f="$T/fx2"
+  mkdir -p "$f"
+  printf 'diff --git "a/.claude/caf\\303\\251.md" "b/.claude/caf\\303\\251.md"\r\n--- "a/.claude/caf\\303\\251.md"\r\n+++ "b/.claude/caf\\303\\251.md"\r\n@@ -1 +1 @@\r\n-a\r\n+b\r\ndiff --git a/.claude/../etc/passwd b/.claude/../etc/passwd\r\ndiff --git a//abs b//abs\r\n' > "$f/head.diff"
+  lib _sm_oracle_py answer-set "$f" "$SRC"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  [ "$(grep -v '^sandbox-mount:' <<<"$output")" = $'pr\t.claude/café.md' ]
+  grep -q "rejected path '.claude/../etc/passwd'" <<<"$output"
+}
+
+@test "overlay head mode (default): PR paths at pr/head/, deleted and old-name paths removed, the symlink never followed, fix-commit path at head_commit, exec bit kept, untouched paths and checksums.json unchanged" {
+  lib overlay_answer_paths "$W" "$FX" head "$SRC" "$F"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  [ "$(content .claude/scripts/mod.sh)" = "mod head" ]
+  [ -x "$W/.claude/scripts/mod.sh" ]
+  [ "$(content .claude/scripts/added.sh)" = "added head" ]
+  [ ! -e "$W/.claude/scripts/deleted.sh" ]
+  [ ! -e "$W/.claude/scripts/old name.sh" ]
+  [ "$(content ".claude/scripts/new name.sh")" = "new name head" ]
+  [ "$(content ".claude/data/x y.txt")" = "xy head" ]
+  [ ! -e "$W/.claude/skills/s1/SKILL.md" ] && [ ! -L "$W/.claude/skills/s1/SKILL.md" ]
+  [ "$(cat "$T/outside-secret")" = "SECRET outside the fixture" ]
+  ! grep -rq SECRET "$W/.claude" || false
+  [ "$(content .claude/scripts/fixonly.sh)" = "fixonly head" ]
+  [ "$(content .claude/checksums.json)" = '{"files":{"later":1}}' ]
+  [ "$(content .claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md)" = "loa" ]
+  [ ! -e "$W/.claude/scripts/evil.sh" ]
+  [ ! -e "$W/lib" ]
+  # evidence, written to ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE as the run's pre-launch record
+  [ "$(ev mount_overlay)" = "head:9" ]
+  [ "$(ev overlay_sha256 | wc -l)" -eq 9 ]
+  [ "$(ev overlay_sha256 | grep -c '=absent$')" -eq 4 ]
+  grep -qx "overlay_sha256=.claude/scripts/mod.sh=$(printf 'mod head\n' | python3 -I -c 'import hashlib,sys; print(hashlib.sha256(sys.stdin.buffer.read()).hexdigest())')" "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE"
+  grep -qx 'overlay_sha256=.claude/data/x y.txt=[0-9a-f]\{64\}' "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE"
+  ! grep -q 'overlay_sha256=.claude/checksums.json' "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE" || false
+  ! grep -q 'overlay_sha256=lib/' "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE" || false
+  [ "$(ev gate_scripts_at_pr_version)" = ".claude/scripts/added.sh,.claude/scripts/fixonly.sh,.claude/scripts/mod.sh,.claude/scripts/new name.sh" ]
+  [ "$(ev copy_source)" = "$F" ]
+  [ "$(ev overlay_removed)" = 4 ]
+  [ "$(ev overlay_fix_commit)" = available ]
+  [ "$(ev overlay_fixture)" = "$FX" ]
+}
+
+@test "overlay base mode: pr/base/ versions, PR-added paths removed, deleted and old-name paths restored at base, fix-commit path still at head_commit" {
+  lib overlay_answer_paths "$W" "$FX" base "$SRC"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  [ "$(content .claude/scripts/mod.sh)" = "mod base" ]
+  [ ! -x "$W/.claude/scripts/mod.sh" ]
+  [ ! -e "$W/.claude/scripts/added.sh" ]
+  [ ! -e "$W/.claude/scripts/new name.sh" ]
+  [ "$(content .claude/scripts/deleted.sh)" = "deleted base" ]
+  [ "$(content ".claude/scripts/old name.sh")" = "old name base" ]
+  [ "$(content ".claude/data/x y.txt")" = "xy base" ]
+  [ "$(content .claude/scripts/fixonly.sh)" = "fixonly head" ]
+  [ "$(ev mount_overlay)" = "base:9" ]
+  [ "$(ev gate_scripts_at_pr_version)" = ".claude/scripts/deleted.sh,.claude/scripts/fixonly.sh,.claude/scripts/mod.sh,.claude/scripts/old name.sh" ]
+}
+
+@test "overlay: an unknown fix commit logs fix_commit_unavailable and continues with the PR paths" {
+  sed -i "s/^fix_commit: .*/fix_commit: \"$(printf 'e%.0s' $(seq 1 40))\"/" "$FX/fixture.yaml"
+  lib overlay_answer_paths "$W" "$FX" head "$SRC"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  grep -q 'fix_commit_unavailable eeeeeeee' <<<"$output"
+  [ "$(ev mount_overlay)" = "head:8" ]
+  [ "$(ev overlay_fix_commit)" = unavailable ]
+  [ "$(content .claude/scripts/fixonly.sh)" = "fixonly LATER fixed" ]   # not an answer path without the fix commit
+  [ "$(content .claude/scripts/mod.sh)" = "mod head" ]
+  lib check_mount_closed "$W" "$FX" "$SRC"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}
+
+@test "overlay refusals (exit 2): missing fixture, bad mode, copy_source other than source_commit, a dirty copy source, a symlink component in the sandbox" {
+  lib overlay_answer_paths "$W" "$T/nope" head "$SRC"
+  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]; grep -q 'fixture not found or has no head.diff' <<<"$output"
+  lib overlay_answer_paths "$W" "$FX" later "$SRC"
+  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]; grep -q 'mode must be head or base' <<<"$output"
+  lib overlay_answer_paths "$W" "$FX" head "$SRC" "$H"
+  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]; grep -q "copy_source $F differs from source_commit $H" <<<"$output"
+  [ "$(content .claude/scripts/mod.sh)" = "mod LATER fixed" ]   # nothing overlaid
+  ! grep -q '^mount_overlay=' "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE" || false
+  echo dirty >> "$SRC/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+  lib overlay_answer_paths "$W" "$FX" head "$SRC"
+  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]; grep -q "copy_source=$F-dirty" <<<"$output"
+  git -C "$SRC" checkout -q -- .claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md
+  rm -rf "$W/.claude/data"; mkdir -p "$T/elsewhere"; ln -s "$T/elsewhere" "$W/.claude/data"
+  lib overlay_answer_paths "$W" "$FX" head "$SRC"
+  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]; grep -q 'symlink component .claude/data' <<<"$output"
+  [ -z "$(ls -A "$T/elsewhere")" ]
+}
+
+@test "check_mount_closed: passes on the overlaid sandbox; refuses an unmodified mount, a stray later copy, a mutated path, a second commit, a remote" {
+  lib check_mount_closed "$W" "$FX" "$SRC"

+# make_closed_run — a source repo (head commit H, fix commit F = the pin), a PR fixture and a
+# run dir whose sandbox was materialised and overlaid by the real mount library
+make_closed_run() {
+  local src="$T/c-src" fx="$T/c-fx" rd="$T/c-run" w
+  mkdir -p "$src/.claude/scripts" "$src/.claude/loa"
+  printf 'gate head\n' > "$src/.claude/scripts/gate.sh"
+  printf 'helper head\n' > "$src/.claude/scripts/helper.sh"
+  printf 'loa\n' > "$src/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+  ( cd "$src" && git init -q && gg . add -A && gg . commit -qm head )
+  CH="$(git -C "$src" rev-parse HEAD)"
+  printf 'gate LATER fixed\n' > "$src/.claude/scripts/gate.sh"
+  printf 'helper LATER fixed\n' > "$src/.claude/scripts/helper.sh"
+  ( cd "$src" && gg . add -A && gg . commit -qm fix )
+  CF="$(git -C "$src" rev-parse HEAD)"
+  mkdir -p "$fx/head/.claude/scripts" "$fx/base/.claude/scripts"
+  printf 'gate head\n' > "$fx/head/.claude/scripts/gate.sh"; printf 'gate base\n' > "$fx/base/.claude/scripts/gate.sh"
+  printf 'diff --git a/.claude/scripts/gate.sh b/.claude/scripts/gate.sh\n--- a/.claude/scripts/gate.sh\n+++ b/.claude/scripts/gate.sh\n@@ -1 +1 @@\n-gate base\n+gate head\n' > "$fx/head.diff"
+  printf 'name: pr-c\nhead_commit: "%s"\nfix_commit: "%s"\n' "$CH" "$CF" > "$fx/fixture.yaml"
+  mkdir -p "$rd/meta" "$rd/sandbox/pr" "$rd/eval"
+  w="$rd/sandbox"
+  cp -a "$fx/head" "$fx/base" "$fx/head.diff" "$w/pr/"
+  git -C "$w" init -q; printf '/.claude/\n' >> "$w/.git/info/exclude"; gg "$w" add -A; gg "$w" commit -qm base
+  printf 'base_commit=%s\n' "$(git -C "$w" rev-parse HEAD)" > "$rd/meta/arm-evidence.txt"
+  mkdir -p "$w/.claude"; cp -a "$src/.claude/." "$w/.claude/"
+  ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE="$rd/meta/arm-evidence.txt" bash -c 'source "$1"; overlay_answer_paths "$2" "$3" head "$4" "$5"' _ \
+    "$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh" "$w" "$fx" "$src" "$CF" 2>/dev/null
+  echo a1_closed > "$rd/meta/arm"

2	+#!/usr/bin/env bats
3	+# =============================================================================
4	+# tests/unit/adversarial-review-budget-scale.bats — cycle-131 Sprint 1 Task 1.8 (PRD FR-4, SDD D-4.2).
5	+#
6	+# flatline_protocol.<code_review|security_audit>.budget_scale: fixed | diff (default fixed) and budget_cents_max
7	+# (default 600). With diff the gate's budget is min(max(budget_cents, ceil(estimate × 1.2)), budget_cents_max); an
8	+# estimate above that still refuses (exit 4, status budget_exceeded, reason budget). A malformed scale or maximum
9	+# fails closed to fixed. The envelope names budget_scale / budget_cents_effective / budget_cents_max only when the
10	+# key is written: a config without it writes the envelope it always wrote.
11	+#
12	+# Whole-run harness: adversarial-review-s3-helpers.bash (main() sourced, invoke_dissenter stubbed, no model called).
13	+# Prices: one fixture alias at 100 USD per Mtok input and 0 output, so each voice costs tokens / 100 cents, with
14	+# tokens = diff bytes / 3 + 500 (the gate's own estimate) — 108,300 bytes → 366c, 62,700 → 214c, 208,500 → 700c.
15	+# =============================================================================
16	+
17	+load adversarial-review-s3-helpers
18	+
19	+setup() { export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"; s3_setup sprint-s3bsc; }
20	+teardown() { s3_teardown; }
21	+
22	+_cfg() {  # <gate key> <budget_cents> [extra gate lines] — the gate under test, companion off, one priced primary
23	+    s3_config "hounfour:
24	+  providers:
25	+    openai:
26	+      models:
27	+        fixture-scale:
28	+          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 100000000, output_per_mtok: 0}
29	+flatline_protocol:
30	+  $1:
31	+    enabled: true
32	+    model: fixture-scale
33	+    budget_cents: $2
34	+    timeout_seconds: 30
35	+    companion_voice: false
36	+    fallback_chain: []
37	+${3:-}"
38	+}
39	+
40	+_diff_of() {  # <bytes> → $T/diff.patch of exactly that size (a header and one long line)
41	+    { printf 'diff --git a/x.sh b/x.sh\n'; head -c $(( $1 - 25 )) /dev/zero | tr '\0' 'a'; } > "$T/diff.patch"
42	+    [ "$(wc -c < "$T/diff.patch" | tr -d ' ')" -eq "$1" ]
43	+}
44	+
45	+@test "BSC-1 the key absent: the shipped gate, byte for byte — estimate 366c over budget 200c is refused and the envelope names no scaling" {
46	+    _diff_of 108300
47	+    _cfg code_review 200
48	+    result=$(s3_run review)
49	+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
50	+    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.status' <<<"$result")" = "budget_exceeded" ]
51	+    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "366" ]
52	+    [ "$(jq '.metadata.budget_cents' <<<"$result")" = "200" ]
53	+    # exactly the keys the gate wrote before cycle-131
54	+    [ "$(jq -c '.metadata | keys' <<<"$result")" = '["budget_cents","estimate_voices","estimated_cents","status","type"]' ]
55	+    grep -qF "Estimated cost (366c) exceeds budget (200c)" "$T/stderr.log"
56	+    ! grep -q "budget_scale" "$T/stderr.log" || { echo "an absent key was said"; return 1; }
57	+    [ ! -s "$CALLS" ]
58	+}
59	+
60	+@test "BSC-2 budget_scale: fixed written explicitly keeps the configured budget (366c over 200c refused) and names the scaling, reason budget" {

66	+      = '{"status":"budget_exceeded","reason":"budget","budget_scale":"fixed","budget_cents":200,"budget_cents_effective":200,"budget_cents_max":600,"estimated_cents":366}' ]
67	+    [ ! -s "$CALLS" ]
68	+}

88	+      = '{"status":"budget_exceeded","reason":"budget","budget_scale":"diff","budget_cents":200,"budget_cents_effective":600,"budget_cents_max":600,"estimated_cents":700}' ]

101	+    result=$(s3_run review)
102	+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ]
103	+    [ "$(jq -c '.metadata | {reason, budget_cents_effective, budget_cents_max}' <<<"$result")" = '{"reason":"budget","budget_cents_effective":210,"budget_cents_max":210}' ]
104	+}

106	+@test "BSC-5 a malformed budget_scale fails closed to fixed and is said: 366c over 200c is refused whatever the spelling (Diff, yes, a list, a map)" {
107	+    _diff_of 108300
108	+    local v

114	+        [ "$(jq '.metadata.budget_cents_effective' <<<"$result")" = "200" ]
115	+        grep -q "WARN: flatline_protocol.code_review.budget_scale=.* is not fixed or diff — fixed applies" "$T/stderr.log" || { echo "budget_scale: $v not said"; return 1; }

128	+        [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.budget_scale' <<<"$result")" = "fixed" ]
129	+        [ "$(jq '.metadata.budget_cents_effective' <<<"$result")" = "200" ]
130	+        grep -qF "is not a whole number — budget_scale fixed applies" "$T/stderr.log" || { echo "budget_cents_max: $v not said"; return 1; }
131	+    done
